claim_text: Airbyte says it identified a security incident in which an attacker had access to its systems
summary: Airbyte's own status page says it 'identified a security incident' and that its security team 'detected the attack, blocked it, and took Airbyte Cloud offline, preventing the attacker from maintaining access to our systems.'
detail: Airbyte posted this on its status page at 4:09 PM ET on Nov 17 (21:09 UTC) and on its own X account. The statement covers Airbyte Cloud; it does not mention self-managed Airbyte. It is the company's account; no outside investigator has confirmed it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Airbyte's own status page (Tier 1) states it; three trackers relay the same words.

claim_text: Airbyte believes the incident is part of a broader, global cyberattack
summary: Airbyte says it 'believe[s]' the incident is 'part of a broader, global cyberattack.' It has not said which attack it means or who else was hit.
detail: That Airbyte holds this belief is on its status page. Whether other organizations were hit by the same attacker is Airbyte's belief only; we found no other source that names the wider attack.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Only Airbyte makes the claim, and it is a belief it did not back up; trackers repeat it.
notes: Held at Reported: a company's unexplained belief about a wider attack is not independent evidence.

claim_text: Airbyte took Airbyte Cloud offline after the incident, and users saw HTTP 502 errors
summary: Airbyte's status incident opened at 6:22 AM ET on Nov 17 for failing data syncs; users then saw 'Airbyte is temporarily unavailable (HTTP 502)'. Airbyte took Cloud offline and said it would stay down until it was confident it was safe.
detail: The status page shows the 6:22 AM ET opening, the 8:39 AM ET note about 502 errors and the hourly 'continue to be patient' updates through Nov 18.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Airbyte's status page and X posts (Tier 1 and 4) give the steps; two trackers repeat them.

claim_text: Airbyte says fewer than 1% of its customers were affected and that it contacted each of them directly
summary: Airbyte says 'fewer than 1% of our customers were affected, and we have already contacted each of them directly.' It has not said what the attacker reached at those customers.
detail: This is Airbyte's own figure and no outside party has checked it. It counts customers, not data or records, and Airbyte did not say how many customers there are.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Airbyte's status page states the figure (Tier 1); it is a company statement we cannot check.
notes: Confirmed that Airbyte said it, not that the number is independently verified.

claim_text: Customer data was accessed or taken
summary: Airbyte has not said whether the attacker reached customer data, credentials or metadata. The trackers say the same.
detail: Airbyte says it contacted the affected customers. It has not said what they were told. No outlet or customer has published what was reached.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source says what the attacker reached; Airbyte's statements are silent on it.

claim_text: A named group or person is behind the attack
summary: No one has named an attacker. Airbyte says 'the attacker' only, and we found no claim of responsibility or ransom demand in press or tracker coverage.
detail: Under MANUAL.md 2.11.1 an actor needs a government or credible independent analysis to be Confirmed. None exists. We did not visit any leak site.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Airbyte and the trackers say no attacker has been named.

claim_text: The root cause: how the attacker got in
summary: Airbyte has not published how the attacker got in or what failed. Its own X post says it will publish a full incident report once its security team finalizes it.
detail: The status page gives no cause. The report promise is in Airbyte's own X post of Nov 20 (Tier 4). No closure without a published cause.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The official page names no cause; the promised report was not out when we checked.
notes: The promised full incident report would settle this.

claim_text: As of 12:47 PM ET Nov 23, Airbyte said 16 API connectors, Connector Builder and MCP were still down 'as a cautionary measure'
summary: Airbyte now says its Nov 21 note that Intercom was fixed 'was made in error' and that '16 API Connectors remain down due to OAuth being deactivated', including Salesforce, HubSpot, Intercom and Zendesk. Builder and MCP stay down.
detail: The 16: Salesforce and HubSpot (source and destination), Gong, Harvest, Intercom, Jira, Mailchimp, Retently, Snapchat Marketing, Trello, Uptick, Zendesk Support, Zendesk Sunshine and Zendesk Talk. At 1:00 AM ET Nov 21 Airbyte had said Intercom was fixed and 15 remained down; on Nov 23 it took that back and said to consider Intercom still down. Airbyte says it will restore them and calls keeping Builder and MCP down 'a cautionary measure.' It does not say who deactivated the OAuth or why. The last update on the page when we checked was 12:47 PM ET Nov 23 (17:47 UTC).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Airbyte's own status page (Tier 1) lists the connectors and the time.

claim_text: Airbyte began restoring Cloud on Nov 19, and most data syncs and database connectors were working by Nov 20
summary: Airbyte began 'gradually returning services' at 10:08 PM ET Nov 18, and by 3:05 AM ET Nov 20 said most syncs were operational and database connectors worked while API sources were not. It says Cloud was back online on Nov 20.
detail: The 'Cloud is back online' line is in Airbyte's own X post at 2:54 AM ET on Nov 20 (Tier 4) and echoed by The Weather Report. The status page was still showing a partial outage when we checked.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Airbyte's status page (Tier 1) gives the restore steps; two others repeat them.

claim_text: Salesforce disabled the Airbyte connected app on Nov 20 after 'suspicious activity associated with the third-party provider Airbyte'
summary: Salesforce's security advisory, posted 4:33 PM ET on Nov 20, says it disabled connections from the Airbyte connected app to customers' Salesforce instances as a precaution. It tells customers to contact Airbyte.
detail: The advisory says integrations stay unavailable until Airbyte finishes remediation and shows they can be restored safely. It does not describe the activity.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Salesforce's own Trust Status page (Tier 1) states it.

claim_text: Salesforce says this was not a Salesforce platform problem
summary: The advisory says it 'was not the result of a Salesforce platform service disruption or any vulnerability within the core Salesforce platform.'
detail: This is Salesforce's own statement. It also says it will notify affected customers 'without undue delay' if it finds unauthorized access to their data.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Salesforce's own Trust Status page (Tier 1) states it.

claim_text: Salesforce customer data was accessed through the Airbyte app
summary: Salesforce says only that if it identifies unauthorized access to customer data it will notify customers. It has not said any was accessed.
detail: The advisory was posted Nov 20 and not updated as of our check. A precaution is not a finding.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Salesforce's advisory makes no finding of unauthorized access.

claim_text: Platforms other than Salesforce, such as HubSpot or Zendesk, cut off Airbyte after the incident
summary: Airbyte says those connectors are down because OAuth is deactivated. We found no statement from HubSpot, Intercom, Zendesk or the other platforms saying they did it or why.
detail: Only Salesforce has said it disabled Airbyte's app. For the others, who turned OAuth off is not stated.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Only Salesforce has published a statement; Airbyte's page does not say who acted on the other connectors.

claim_text: The incident is tied to a named attack campaign or to other companies' breaches
summary: No source names the 'broader, global cyberattack' or links Airbyte's incident to another company's breach. Similar patterns in other third-party breaches are not evidence of a link.
detail: Airbyte did not say which attack it means. We did not tie this to any other page on this site.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The trackers say the wider attack is unnamed; no official source ties it to another incident.
